message.content: As the context length increased, the model’s ability to retain and accurately reference earlier information began to degrade, leading to a noticeable decline in coherence and factual consistency. The attention mechanism, which scales quadratically with sequence length, struggled to maintain focus on relevant tokens amid the growing volume of filler text, causing the model to drift from the original intent and produce less precise responses. This degradation manifested as a higher rate of hallucinated details, reduced adherence to instructions, and a general loss of contextual grounding, highlighting the challenges of scaling inference performance under long-prompt conditions.
